newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU opens full probe into Guinness/GdMet deal.
newsitem.headline: EU opens full probe into Guinness/GdMet deal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it had started a full antitrust probe into the proposed merger between Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan.
The 23.8 billion pound ($39.2 billion) merger would create one of the world's largest food and beverages company.

The Commission said in a statement it was concerned about the impact of the merger on the spirits sector, particularly in the whisky market where the combined share was over 40 percent in certain European countries.
It also said that the merger would result in "significant" overlaps in the gin and vodka markets.
"It cannot be excluded at this stage that the merger would give rise to a dominant position in one or more of the markets concerned," it said in a late statement.

The merger would bring under one roof Johnnie Walker and Bell's whisky, Gordon's Gin, Smirnoff Vodka, Guinness's traditional stout, the Burger King fast-food chain, Haagen-Dazs ice-cream and Green Giant canned vegetables.
